name: Bhakra Nangal Project
irrigationAreaHa: 4.0 million hectares (Bhakra Canal System & Sirhind Canal)
features: Built between 1948–1963; described by Jawaharlal Nehru as a Temple of Modern India; one of the highest gravity dams in the world; vital backbone of Green Revolution agriculture in Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan.

name: Tehri Dam Hydroelectric Project
irrigationAreaHa: 2.7 lakh hectares; supplies 300 cusecs drinking water to Delhi-NCR and UP
features: Highest dam in India (5th highest in the world); located in the seismically active Central Himalayan Seismic Gap (Zone V), which prompted extensive environmental campaigns led by Sunderlal Bahuguna (Chipko Movement).

name: Sardar Sarovar Project
reservoir: Sardar Sarovar (375 sq km, 214 km long)
irrigationAreaHa: 1.85 million hectares via 458 km Narmada Main Canal
features: Key lifeline providing drinking water to drought-prone Saurashtra, Kutch, and southern Rajasthan (Barmer/Jalore); power shared between MP (57%), Maharashtra (27%), and Gujarat (16%); Statue of Unity is located 3.2 km downstream on Sadhu Bet island.

name: Hirakud Dam
type: Composite Earthen, Concrete, and Masonry Dam
lengthM: 25.8 km (total dam including dykes; main dam 4.8 km)
reservoir: Hirakud Reservoir (743 sq km — one of Asia's largest artificial lakes)
irrigationAreaHa: 2.35 lakh hectares of Kharif and Rabi paddy in Sambalpur, Bargarh, Subarnapur
features: Constructed 1948–1957 to tame the devastating annual floods of the Mahanadi; longest earthen dam in the world; Gandhi Minar and Nehru Minar provide panoramic reservoir views.

name: Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC)
type: Multipurpose River Basin Authority (modelled on US TVA)
reservoir: Tilaiya, Maithon, Konar, and Panchet reservoirs
irrigationAreaHa: 5.5 lakh hectares in lower Damodar basin (Bardhaman, Hooghly)
features: India's first multipurpose river valley project, established 18 February 1948 by an Act of Constituent Assembly; tamed the Sorrow of Bengal; powers the heavy industrial mineral belt of Asansol-Durgapur-Dhanbad.

name: Nagarjuna Sagar Project
reservoir: Nagarjuna Sagar (285 sq km, 11.47 billion m³ capacity)
irrigationAreaHa: 1.0 million hectares via Jawahar Canal (right bank) and Lal Bahadur Canal (left bank)
features: Built 1955–1967; one of the largest masonry dams in the world; named after the 2nd-century CE Buddhist philosopher Nagarjuna whose ancient vihara ruins on Nagarjunakonda island were relocated to an island museum in the reservoir.

name: Idukki Hydroelectric Project
features: Constructed with Canadian technical aid between the Kuravan and Kurathi granite hills; Asia's first double-curvature arch dam; powerhouse located deep underground inside Nadukani hill at Moolamattom, providing ~30% of Kerala's electric power.

name: Polavaram National Irrigation Project
type: Earth-cum-Rockfill Dam with 48 Radial Spillway Gates
irrigationAreaHa: 2.91 lakh hectares directly + stabilization of 4 lakh ha in Krishna-Godavari deltas
features: Conferred National Project status under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014; enables inter-basin diversion of 80 TMC water from surplus Godavari basin to deficit Krishna basin via Right Main Canal; supplies drinking water to Visakhapatnam steel city.

name: Kosi Project (Bhimnagar Barrage)
irrigationAreaHa: 8.5 lakh hectares in North Bihar and Nepal
features: Constructed under 1954 Indo-Nepal agreement to check avulsion floods of Kosi (Sorrow of Bihar), which shifted westward by >120 km over 250 years.

name: Ken-Betwa Link Project (KBLP)
reservoir: Daudhan Dam reservoir on Ken river
features: Pioneer project under the National Perspective Plan for interlinking of rivers; transfers surplus water from Ken basin to deficit Betwa basin; involves submergence of core habitat in Panna Tiger Reserve.

name: Rihand Dam (Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar)
reservoir: Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar (466 sq km — largest artificial reservoir in India by surface area and volume)
irrigationAreaHa: Supplies cooling and process water to Singrauli industrial belt
features: Located at Pipri in Sonbhadra district, UP; transformed Singrauli into the Energy Capital of India powering massive pithead NTPC super thermal plants and Hindalco aluminium smelter.

name: Tungabhadra Project (Pampa Sagar)
irrigationAreaHa: 5.0 lakh hectares in arid Raichur, Bellary, and Kurnool districts
features: Constructed 1949–1953; early benchmark in inter-state cooperative river basin development; located near the historic Vijayanagara ruins at Hampi.
